newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Peking Apparel poised for strong debut.
newsitem.headline: Peking Apparel poised for strong debut.

text.p: Peking Apparel International Group Ltd shares should make a strong trading debut on Friday as investors want exposure to China's retail market, analysts said.

The leather garments manufacturer offered 64.75 million shares at HK$1.00 per share. The initial public offering was 130.21 times oversubscribed and the stock was quoted at about HK$1.40 in the grey market, analysts said.
"It has strong upside potential because investors may take it as a China retail concept in view of its distribution network in China," said Michael Ng, an analyst at ASG Investment.
The strength of other debuts recently contributed to the overwhelming response for Peking Apparel, analysts said.

Peking Apparel makes and sells leather garments. In its listing prospectus, the company forecast profit after tax but before extraordinary items of not less than HK$35 million for the year ending March 31. It had net profit of HK$27.9 million in the year to March 31, 1996, on turnover of HK$290.90 million.
Sales from the Chinese market accounted for about 54 percent of total 1995/96 turnover.
Stanley Ng, research manager at Mansion House Research, said the company's future prospects would be brighter if the company could find more markets for its products.

Peking Apparel said it would use the net proceeds of about HK$53.8 million from the offering to buy an interest in a tannery and set up representative offices and showrooms in the Chinese cities of Tsingdao, Beijing, Chengdu, Harbin and Guangzhou.
Proceeds would also be used to upgrade manufacturing facilities and to repay bank loans.
